text: The append stores the six fields as references with the legacy types (contact_key varchar(255), from_holder_ref varchar(60), to_holder_ref varchar(60), treatment_id uuid, proceeds_id uuid, retention_class varchar(20)), the retention class is resolved by the service and refused with 422 when the caller supplies one or the event code has no class row, and nothing is written on either refusal.
why: The legacy story added the six columns with those types and resolved the class from a local table, and no source states the response status of an unresolvable class or whether a caller may supply one; a defaulted class would file the entry under a period nobody set.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-034 section 13 'Database' (the six columns and their types), section 8 BR6, section 3 (the ILG-STD assumption), AC1 and AC2; LDM v8 DF-INT-022 to DF-INT-029; RWB-P1-E1066-APP section 12.1 (422 MSG-GEN-001 for a missing required value).
confirm: Solution architect with the data architect
impact: If a caller-supplied class is allowed instead, the validator and AC2 change; the migration, the keys and the trigger are unaffected.

text: The interaction ledger of rwb-source-data is published as POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions and GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions, and the flat POST /interactions of RWB-P1-E1066-APP is realigned to the case-scoped form.
why: The Ownership Map is the authority for the operations a service provides and lists the case-scoped form, which is also the form the consumer contract of this key fakes; the case in the address carries the case check and the scope, and two addresses for one resource cannot both stand.
read: Ownership Map v1 P1 rows; RWB-P2-E2034-CON section 12.2; RWB-P1-E1066-APP section 12.1; RWB-P1-E1068-APP section 12.1; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-13 and DP-18.
confirm: Solution architect with the P1 squad
impact: The writer story and its contract must publish the same path family; this story's own code is unaffected because it publishes section 12.1 as written.

text: Every event code of LOV-LEDGER-EVENT carries the retention class ILG-STD until Compliance sets the periods (DL26), and LOV-LEDGER-EVENT carries the two values PARTNER_RESULT and OFFER that the legacy story adds; both are fixture values and neither is written in code.
why: The legacy story records the class per event code and adds two event codes, and Compliance has not set the periods; a value in code would be a business value in code, and an unlisted code would be refused by the validator.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-034 section 3 (DL26, the ILG-STD assumption, the two added values), section 8 BR6, section 13 'Configuration and reference data'; LDM v8 LOV-LEDGER-EVENT; RWB-P1-E1066-APP section 1 (the list it publishes).
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer with the reference data administrator
impact: When the periods are set, a reference-data version replaces the fixture with no code change and no migration; an entry filed under ILG-STD may need a class restatement that is a new entry, because the ledger is append only.

text: The holder reference is written as USER:<user id> or PARTNER:<partner code>, the contact key as <contact type>:<contact key>, and both are validated as formats and never resolved into a name or a number by this service.
why: The legacy criteria write the holder and contact key in exactly those forms, and no source fixes them as a schema rule; the store must accept them without reading the record they name.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-034 AC1 ('PHONE:CP-SYN-0301-M'), AC2 ('USER:U-2001' to 'USER:U-2002'), BR2, BR5, section 11; LDM v8 DF-EXT-013 (contact_key composite contact_type:key) and DF-INT-023, DF-INT-024.
confirm: Solution architect with the P1 and S9 squads
impact: A caller that sends another form is refused with MSG-GEN-001 naming the field; if a form changes, the validator and AC3 change and the stored rows keep the form they were written with.

text: The case read returns entries ordered by occurred_at and then by case_seq, filters on channel, actor and date range, and pages with the size and maximum that RWB-P1-E1068-APP reads as parameters from the rwb-case parameters contract.
why: The legacy story fixes the order (BR9) and the filters but states no page size, and this story extends a read that already owns its paging; a second default here would publish two answers for one read.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-034 section 4 step 9 to 10, section 8 BR9, AC3, AC9; RWB-P1-E1068-APP section 12.1 (size default 50, maximum 200, read through the parameters contract of DP-06).
confirm: Solution architect with the P1 squad
impact: No new parameter and no build dependency; a change of the default is a parameter version of rwb-case and no code change here.

text: The event-code list, the retention class rows and the Case record C and R answers are read through the reference-data client library of DP-07 and the authorise guard library of DP-08 with fixtures until those contracts are published, and a read that does not answer inside 2 s refuses the call and writes nothing.
why: The Work Package lists RWB-P2-E2034-CON as the only contract dependency and names no reference-data or authorise contract, while the values must not be constants in code and the class must never be guessed.
read: Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-07 and DP-08; RWB-P1-E1068-APP sections 12.2 and 12.8 (the same two libraries and fixtures); LDM v8 LOV-LEDGER-EVENT.
confirm: Solution architect with the P1 squad
impact: No build dependency and no blocking call; when the contracts land the fixture is dropped and the lists are read with their version.

text: delivery_status and external_ref of a letter or a message entry are not columns of this story and not values it resolves: the comms slices of this key write them through this append, and the store returns them as the writer of RWB-P1-E1066-APP stored them.
why: The legacy story reads the delivery status and the barcode from the notice and writes them on the entry, while the target splits dispatch and proof of delivery across the comms slices; no source states which slice owns the two columns for wave 2.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-034 AC4, section 11 (DF-INT-028, DF-INT-029), section 12 and section 19; LDM v8 DF-INT-028 and DF-INT-029; RWB-P1-E2021-APP sections 1 and 12.1; RWB-P1-E2022-APP fingerprint.
confirm: Solution architect with the P6 squad
impact: If the two columns become this story's, the migration grows by two columns and the migration version is re-planned; no key or trigger changes.

text: The EFS contact-outcome rows of a business date are read by RWB-P1-E2001-APP and reach this store as an append under the key EFS:<efs_record_key>, and the contact-fact read behind a contact key is a sibling operation of this service that this story does not own or redefine.
why: The legacy story read both in process inside one module; under D-RCV-60 the EFS history read is RWB-P1-E2001-APP's, and the consumer contract names the contact read by its legacy interface only, so the store must not absorb either read.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-034 section 4 step 4, section 12, section 13; RWB-P1-E2001-APP section 1 and section 12.1; RWB-P2-E2034-CON section 12.2.
confirm: Solution architect with the P1 squad
impact: If the contact read lands in this story, section 12.1 gains an operation and AC1 gains a case; the six columns, the keys and the trigger are unaffected.
